readme.text:
# Shopware CLI

[![Hosted By: Cloudsmith](https://img.shields.io/badge/OSS%20hosting%20by-cloudsmith-blue?logo=cloudsmith&style=flat-square)](https://cloudsmith.com)

Shopware CLI is a command line companion for common Shopware account, project, and extension workflows.

## Table of Contents

- [What it helps with](#what-it-helps-with)
- [Highlights](#highlights)
- [Install](#install)
- [Usage](#usage)
- [Repository Layout](#repository-layout)
- [Documentation](#documentation)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
- [License](#license)

## What it helps with

Use this CLI when you want to manage Shopware accounts, build and validate extensions, automate project maintenance, or run everyday developer tasks without leaving the terminal.

## Highlights

- Account-related commands under `shopware-cli account`
- Extension build, validation, formatting, changelog, and packaging helpers
- Project automation commands for create, config, cache, admin, and CI workflows
- Interactive terminal support, plus a non-interactive mode for scripts and CI

## Install

### From source with Go

```bash
go install github.com/shopware/shopware-cli@latest
```

### Build locally from this repository

```bash
git clone https://github.com/shopware/shopware-cli.git
cd shopware-cli
go build -o bin/shopware-cli .
```

## Usage

Show the available commands:

```bash
shopware-cli --help
```

Common command groups:

```bash
shopware-cli account --help
shopware-cli extension --help
shopware-cli project --help
```

If you need CI-friendly behavior, disable prompts:

```bash
shopware-cli --no-interaction <command>
```

## Repository Layout

- `cmd/`: Cobra command groups for account, extension, and project workflows
- `internal/`: implementation packages for APIs, build steps, validation, TUI, and utilities
- `.github/`: automation and workflow definitions
- `scripts/`: repository helper scripts
- `env-bridge/`: environment bridge helper entrypoint

## Documentation

- Official docs: <https://developer.shopware.com/docs/products/cli/>

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome. If you want to improve commands, docs, or developer workflows, open an issue or send a pull request.

## License

See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

readme.text:
![mirrord logo](./images/logo.svg)
[![Community Slack](https://img.shields.io/badge/Join-e5f7f7?logo=slack&label=Community%20Slack)](https://metalbear.co/slack) [![Github CI](https://github.com/metalbear-co/mirrord/actions/workflows/ci.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/metalbear-co/mirrord/actions/workflows/ci.yaml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)](https://github.com/metalbear-co/mirrord/blob/main/LICENSE) [![GitHub release (latest SemVer)](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/metalbear-co/mirrord)](https://github.com/metalbear-co/mirrord/releases) [![Twitter Follow](https://img.shields.io/twitter/follow/metalbearco?style=social)](https://twitter.com/metalbearco) [mirrord lets developers and AI coding agents run local processes in the context of their Kubernetes environment](https://metalbear.co/mirrord/). It’s meant to provide the benefits of running your service on a cloud environment (e.g. staging) without actually going through the hassle of deploying it there, and without disrupting the environment by deploying untested code. It comes as a Visual Studio Code extension, an IntelliJ plugin and a CLI tool. [You can read more about it here](https://metalbear.co/mirrord/docs/overview/introduction/). **Adopted by**: monday.com, SurveyMonkey, Cadence, CoLab, Daylight Security, Zooplus, and [others](./ADOPTERS.md). # Contents - [Contents](#contents) - [Getting Started](#getting-started) - [VS Code Extension](#vs-code-extension) - [Installation](#installation) - [How To Use](#how-to-use) - [IntelliJ Plugin](#intellij-plugin) - [Installation](#installation-1) - [How To Use](#how-to-use-1) - [CLI Tool](#cli-tool) - [Installation](#installation-2) - [How To Use](#how-to-use-2) - [How It Works](#how-it-works) - [Additional capabilities](#additional-capabilities) - [Using mirrord with AI coding agents](#using-mirrord-with-ai-coding-agents) - [FAQ](#faq) - [Contributing](#contributing) - [Help and Community](#help-and-community) - [Code of Conduct](#code-of-conduct) - [License](#license) --- ## Getting Started - [VS Code Extension](#vs-code-extension) - [IntelliJ Plugin](#intellij-plugin) - [CLI Tool](#cli-tool) > mirrord uses your machine's default kubeconfig for access to the Kubernetes API. --- ## VS Code Extension ### Installation [Get the extension here](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=MetalBear.mirrord). ### How To Use - Click "Enable mirrord" on the status bar - Start debugging your project - Choose pod to impersonate - The debugged process will be plugged into the selected pod by mirrord

--- ## IntelliJ Plugin ### Installation [Get the plugin here](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/plugin/19772-mirrord). ### How To Use - Click the mirrord icon in the Navigation Toolbar - Start debugging your project - Choose a namespace and pod to impersonate - The debugged process will be plugged into the selected pod by mirrord

--- ## CLI Tool ### Installation You can use either ```sh brew install metalbear-co/mirrord/mirrord ``` or ```sh curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/metalbear-co/mirrord/main/scripts/install.sh | bash ``` or using Nix (not official, community maintained): ```sh # Using nix-env (legacy) nix-env -iA nixpkgs.mirrord # Using nix profile (recommended) nix profile install nixpkgs#mirrord ``` or on Windows using Chocolatey: ```sh choco install --pre mirrord ``` ### How To Use ```sh mirrord exec --target ``` e.g. ```sh mirrord exec node app.js --target pod/my-pod ``` --- ## How It Works When you select a pod to impersonate, mirrord launches a pod on the same node as the pod you selected. The new pod is then used to connect your local process and the impersonated pod: it mirrors incoming traffic from the pod to your process, routes outgoing traffic from your process through the pod, and does the same for file reads, file writes, and environment variables. [You can read more about it here](https://metalbear.co/mirrord/docs/overview/introduction/). ### Additional capabilities Container run inside the pod launched by mirrord requires additional [Linux capabilities](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/capabilities.7.html): - `CAP_NET_ADMIN` and `CAP_NET_RAW` - for modifying routing tables - `CAP_SYS_PTRACE` - for reading target pod environment - `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` - for joining target pod network namespace However, you can disable any subset of those in the [configuration](https://metalbear.co/mirrord/docs/reference/configuration/). This will possibly limit mirrord functionalities or even make it unusable in some setups. ```bash MIRRORD_AGENT_DISABLED_CAPABILITIES=CAP_NET_RAW,CAP_SYS_PTRACE mirrord exec node app.js --target pod/my-pod ```

## Using mirrord with AI coding agents mirrord works first-class with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, and other AI coding agents, letting them run and verify generated code against real cluster services without deploying. For setup guides and ready-made workflow skills, see [metalbear-co/skills](https://github.com/metalbear-co/skills) or the [mirrord for AI Agents](https://metalbear.com/mirrord/ai) page. ## FAQ [Our FAQ is available here](https://metalbear.co/mirrord/docs/faq/general/). If you have a question that's not on there, feel free to ask in our [Discussions](https://github.com/metalbear-co/mirrord/discussions) or on [Slack](https://metalbear.co/slack). ## Contributing Contributions are very welcome. Start by checking out our [open issues](https://github.com/metalbear-co/mirrord/issues), and by going through our [contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.md). We're available on [Slack](https://metalbear.co/slack) for any questions. ## Help and Community Join our [Slack](https://metalbear.co/slack) for questions, support and fun. We always appreciate hearing how mirrord has made a difference for our users. Check out our [ADOPTERS.md](./ADOPTERS.md) to see how others are using mirrord — and [open a pull request](https://github.com/metalbear-co/mirrord/pulls) to add your organization if you’d like to share how mirrord has been useful to you. ## Code of Conduct We take our community seriously and we are dedicated to providing a safe and welcoming environment for everyone. Please take a few minutes to review our [Code of Conduct](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). ## License [MIT](./LICENSE)

### Added

- Added `feature.preview.ttl_secs` and `feature.db_branches[].ttl_mins` so each
  feature accepts the TTL in either unit. Setting both `ttl_secs` and
  `ttl_mins` on the same item is rejected.
- Added clarifications for Windows-specific `fs` mapping and `fs` filter quirks
- Document jq filtering support for GCP Pub/Sub in the configuration docs.


### Changed

- In mirrord-up, renamed `mode` to `default_mode` and added a CLI argument to
  set it.


### Fixed

- Agent now falls back to an IPv4 client listener when setting up the
  dual-stack IPv6 one fails (e.g. on clusters with IPv6 disabled).
- Fixed `getaddrinfo` truncating IPv6 addresses resolved through the agent.
- Fixed outgoing connections to path-addressed Unix sockets failing with a "not
  found" error when the agent runs as an ephemeral container.
- The agent no longer logs a spurious warning when a DNS server returns an
  error response code, and layer no longer logs bogus DNS errors with error
  level.

### Fixed

- Fixed remote Unix socket connections failing for some applications, including
  when the socket lives in a directory mounted into the target pod.
- `mirrord ui` no longer drops operator sessions whose `user` field doesn't
  match the `username/k8s_username@hostname` format. Falls back to the raw user
  string for both fields, so synthetic owners like preview environments surface
  in the session list.

![mirrord logo](./images/logo.svg)
[![Community Slack](https://img.shields.io/badge/Join-e5f7f7?logo=slack&label=Community%20Slack)](https://metalbear.co/slack) [![Github CI](https://github.com/metalbear-co/mirrord/actions/workflows/ci.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/metalbear-co/mirrord/actions/workflows/ci.yaml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)](https://github.com/metalbear-co/mirrord/blob/main/LICENSE) [![GitHub release (latest SemVer)](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/metalbear-co/mirrord)](https://github.com/metalbear-co/mirrord/releases) [![Twitter Follow](https://img.shields.io/twitter/follow/metalbearco?style=social)](https://twitter.com/metalbearco) [mirrord lets developers and AI coding agents run local processes in the context of their Kubernetes environment](https://metalbear.co/mirrord/). It’s meant to provide the benefits of running your service on a cloud environment (e.g. staging) without actually going through the hassle of deploying it there, and without disrupting the environment by deploying untested code. It comes as a Visual Studio Code extension, an IntelliJ plugin and a CLI tool. [You can read more about it here](https://metalbear.co/mirrord/docs/overview/introduction/). **Adopted by**: monday.com, SurveyMonkey, Cadence, CoLab, Daylight Security, Zooplus, and [others](./ADOPTERS.md). # Contents - [Contents](#contents) - [Getting Started](#getting-started) - [VS Code Extension](#vs-code-extension) - [Installation](#installation) - [How To Use](#how-to-use) - [IntelliJ Plugin](#intellij-plugin) - [Installation](#installation-1) - [How To Use](#how-to-use-1) - [CLI Tool](#cli-tool) - [Installation](#installation-2) - [How To Use](#how-to-use-2) - [How It Works](#how-it-works) - [Additional capabilities](#additional-capabilities) - [Using mirrord with AI coding agents](#using-mirrord-with-ai-coding-agents) - [FAQ](#faq) - [Contributing](#contributing) - [Help and Community](#help-and-community) - [Code of Conduct](#code-of-conduct) - [License](#license) --- ## Getting Started - [VS Code Extension](#vs-code-extension) - [IntelliJ Plugin](#intellij-plugin) - [CLI Tool](#cli-tool) > mirrord uses your machine's default kubeconfig for access to the Kubernetes API. --- ## VS Code Extension ### Installation [Get the extension here](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=MetalBear.mirrord). ### How To Use - Click "Enable mirrord" on the status bar - Start debugging your project - Choose pod to impersonate - The debugged process will be plugged into the selected pod by mirrord

--- ## IntelliJ Plugin ### Installation [Get the plugin here](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/plugin/19772-mirrord). ### How To Use - Click the mirrord icon in the Navigation Toolbar - Start debugging your project - Choose a namespace and pod to impersonate - The debugged process will be plugged into the selected pod by mirrord

--- ## CLI Tool ### Installation You can use either ```sh brew install metalbear-co/mirrord/mirrord ``` or ```sh curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/metalbear-co/mirrord/main/scripts/install.sh | bash ``` or using Nix (not official, community maintained): ```sh # Using nix-env (legacy) nix-env -iA nixpkgs.mirrord # Using nix profile (recommended) nix profile install nixpkgs#mirrord ``` or on Windows using Chocolatey: ```sh choco install --pre mirrord ``` ### How To Use ```sh mirrord exec --target ``` e.g. ```sh mirrord exec node app.js --target pod/my-pod ``` --- ## How It Works When you select a pod to impersonate, mirrord launches a pod on the same node as the pod you selected. The new pod is then used to connect your local process and the impersonated pod: it mirrors incoming traffic from the pod to your process, routes outgoing traffic from your process through the pod, and does the same for file reads, file writes, and environment variables. [You can read more about it here](https://metalbear.co/mirrord/docs/overview/introduction/). ### Additional capabilities Container run inside the pod launched by mirrord requires additional [Linux capabilities](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/capabilities.7.html): - `CAP_NET_ADMIN` and `CAP_NET_RAW` - for modifying routing tables - `CAP_SYS_PTRACE` - for reading target pod environment - `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` - for joining target pod network namespace However, you can disable any subset of those in the [configuration](https://metalbear.co/mirrord/docs/reference/configuration/). This will possibly limit mirrord functionalities or even make it unusable in some setups. ```bash MIRRORD_AGENT_DISABLED_CAPABILITIES=CAP_NET_RAW,CAP_SYS_PTRACE mirrord exec node app.js --target pod/my-pod ```

## Using mirrord with AI coding agents mirrord works first-class with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, and other AI coding agents, letting them run and verify generated code against real cluster services without deploying. For setup guides and ready-made workflow skills, see [metalbear-co/skills](https://github.com/metalbear-co/skills) or the [mirrord for AI Agents](https://metalbear.com/mirrord/ai) page. ## FAQ [Our FAQ is available here](https://metalbear.co/mirrord/docs/faq/general/). If you have a question that's not on there, feel free to ask in our [Discussions](https://github.com/metalbear-co/mirrord/discussions) or on [Slack](https://metalbear.co/slack). ## Contributing Contributions are very welcome. Start by checking out our [open issues](https://github.com/metalbear-co/mirrord/issues), and by going through our [contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.md). We're available on [Slack](https://metalbear.co/slack) for any questions. ## Help and Community Join our [Slack](https://metalbear.co/slack) for questions, support and fun. We always appreciate hearing how mirrord has made a difference for our users. Check out our [ADOPTERS.md](./ADOPTERS.md) to see how others are using mirrord — and [open a pull request](https://github.com/metalbear-co/mirrord/pulls) to add your organization if you’d like to share how mirrord has been useful to you. ## Code of Conduct We take our community seriously and we are dedicated to providing a safe and welcoming environment for everyone. Please take a few minutes to review our [Code of Conduct](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). ## License [MIT](./LICENSE)

items.body_excerpt:
### Added

- Added `feature.preview.ttl_secs` and `feature.db_branches[].ttl_mins` so each
  feature accepts the TTL in either unit. Setting both `ttl_secs` and
  `ttl_mins` on the same item is rejected.
- Added clarifications for Windows-specific `fs` mapping and `fs` filter quirks
- Document jq filtering support for GCP Pub/Sub in the configuration docs.


### Changed

- In mirrord-up, renamed `mode` to `default_mode` and added a CLI argument to
  set it.


### Fixed

- Agent now falls back to an IPv4 client listener when setting up the
  dual-stack IPv6 one fails (e.g. on clusters with IPv6 disabled).
- Fixed `getaddrinfo` truncating IPv6 addresses resolved through the agent.
- Fixed outgoing connections to path-addressed Unix sockets failing with a "not
  found" error when the agent runs as an ephemeral container.
- The agent no longer logs a spurious warning when a DNS server returns an
  error response code, and layer no longer logs bogus DNS errors with error
  level.

### Fixed

- Fixed remote Unix socket connections failing for some applications, including
  when the socket lives in a directory mounted into the target pod.
- `mirrord ui` no longer drops operator sessions whose `user` field doesn't
  match the `username/k8s_username@hostname` format. Falls back to the raw user
  string for both fields, so synthetic owners like preview environments surface
  in the session list.

scout.summary: The shopware-cli is an active Go-based CLI tool for managing Shopware 6 accounts, extensions, and projects. It supports developer workflows including extension validation, project automation, and CI integration, with recent feature additions around telemetry, Docker compatibility, and configuration flexibility.
highlights: Official CLI companion for Shopware 6 covering account, extension, and project workflows [ID:E-RD-002][ID:E-RD-004].
Recent releases include new features like custom PHP linting, telemetry tracking, and staging mode support [ID:E-RL-001].
Repository includes Dockerfiles and environment bridge tools, indicating containerized development support [ID:E-RF-001][ID:E-RD-008].
Structured codebase with Cobra commands and modular internal packages for APIs, validation, and TUI [ID:E-RD-008].
risks: Open issue suggests evolving Docker-based development workflow may lack documentation or stability [ID:E-IS-002].
Closed issue indicates past limitations in configuration override behavior, possibly affecting user flexibility [ID:E-IS-001].

inventor.summary: The shopware-cli is a Go-based command-line tool designed to streamline Shopware 6 development workflows, offering modular command groups for account management, extension handling, and project automation, with recent innovations in telemetry, Docker compatibility, and configuration extensibility.
highlights: Introduces telemetry features tracking upgrade checks and environment flags (e.g., Elasticsearch, AMQP) to inform product evolution [ID:E-RL-001].
Enables custom PHP version selection for extension linting, enhancing developer flexibility in multi-PHP environments [ID:E-RL-001].
Adds staging mode support in deployment configurations, allowing clearer separation between development and production contexts [ID:E-RL-001].
Implements structured CLI architecture using Cobra with dedicated command groups (account, extension, project) and internal utilities for APIs, validation, and TUI [ID:E-RD-008].
risks: Configuration rigidity observed in past versions (e.g., inability to overwrite dump defaults) may indicate incomplete override mechanisms, potentially limiting customization [ID:E-IS-001].
Emerging Docker-based development workflows remain undocumented or unstable, as noted in open discussions about integration with shopware-cli [ID:E-IS-002].

engineer.summary: The shopware-cli is a Go-based CLI tool that provides structured, modular commands for Shopware 6 account, extension, and project management, with active development focused on developer experience, Docker compatibility, and telemetry integration.
highlights: Built with Go and uses Cobra for command organization, with clear separation into account, extension, and project command groups [ID:E-RD-008][ID:E-RF-001].
Supports containerized development via multiple Dockerfiles (Dockerfile, Dockerfile.base, etc.) and an env-bridge utility [ID:E-RF-001][ID:E-RD-008].
Recent features enhance developer flexibility: custom PHP linting versions, staging mode in deployments, and improved error messaging for setup issues [ID:E-RL-001][ID:E-RL-002].
Includes telemetry for upgrade checks and environment flags (Elasticsearch, AMQP), aiding usage analytics without compromising core functionality [ID:E-RL-001].
risks: An open issue indicates ongoing instability or lack of documentation around Docker-based development workflows, which could hinder adoption [ID:E-IS-002].
Past limitations in configuration override (e.g., dump.rewrite not allowing default overwrites) suggest potential inflexibility in certain automation scenarios [ID:E-IS-001].

skeptic.summary: While shopware-cli presents itself as a robust CLI for Shopware 6 workflows, closer inspection reveals potential gaps in configuration flexibility, immature Docker integration, and telemetry additions that may prioritize vendor insight over user control.
highlights: Telemetry features track upgrade checks and environment flags without clear opt-out documentation, raising transparency concerns [ID:E-RL-001].
Past inability to overwrite dump defaults suggests limited configurability in automation scenarios, undermining claims of workflow flexibility [ID:E-IS-001].
Open issue on Docker-based development indicates the recommended containerized workflow may be unstable or poorly documented [ID:E-IS-002].
risks: Telemetry is being added incrementally (e.g., 'from_version' tags, environment flags) without evident user consent mechanisms or privacy disclosures [ID:E-RL-001].
Configuration rigidity—such as the historical dump.rewrite limitation—may persist in other areas, reducing reliability for scripted or CI use cases [ID:E-IS-001].
Despite multiple Dockerfiles, the lack of stable, documented Docker workflows could mislead developers into adopting an unsupported setup [ID:E-IS-002][ID:E-RF-001].

scout.summary: mirrord is a mature, actively maintained Rust-based developer tool that enables local processes to operate within a remote Kubernetes environment, offering IDE integrations (VS Code, IntelliJ) and CLI support. It is adopted by notable companies and supports AI coding agents, with recent releases addressing networking, Unix socket, and platform-specific issues.
highlights: Enables local development in the context of remote Kubernetes clusters without deployment
Available as VS Code extension, IntelliJ plugin, and CLI tool
Adopted by companies like monday.com, SurveyMonkey, and Cadence
Actively developed with frequent releases fixing networking, DNS, and platform quirks
Supports AI coding agents and integrates with kubeconfig for cluster access
risks: Open issue indicates lack of Windows ARM64 support, limiting cross-platform compatibility
Heavy reliance on Kubernetes may constrain use outside cloud-native environments

inventor.summary: mirrord is an innovative developer tool that virtualizes local execution into a remote Kubernetes environment, enabling seamless access to cluster resources like env vars, DNS, and network traffic without deployment. It uniquely supports AI coding agents and offers multi-IDE integration with robust recent enhancements in networking and platform compatibility.
highlights: Invents a novel 'local-in-cluster' execution model by proxying local processes through a Kubernetes pod via agent-side interception
First-class support for AI coding agents, allowing them to operate with real cloud context during code generation and testing
Multi-platform IDE support (VS Code, IntelliJ) plus CLI enables flexible developer workflows across environments
Recent innovations include dual-stack IPv6/IPv4 fallback, TTL configuration flexibility, and Unix socket handling in ephemeral containers
Uses kubeconfig natively, eliminating custom auth setup and integrating smoothly into existing Kubernetes workflows
risks: Lack of Windows ARM64 support (open issue) limits adoption on emerging hardware platforms
Deep coupling with Kubernetes may hinder applicability in non-containerized or hybrid infrastructure scenarios

engineer.summary: mirrord is a Rust-based tool that enables local processes to run within the context of a remote Kubernetes cluster by leveraging an agent-based architecture, with strong IDE integrations and recent fixes improving networking reliability and platform support.
highlights: Built in Rust with a modular structure including CLI, IDE extensions, and agent components
Uses kubeconfig natively for Kubernetes API access, simplifying authentication and integration
Recent releases fixed critical issues: IPv6 address truncation, Unix socket connectivity, and dual-stack listener fallbacks
Supports ephemeral containers and handles edge cases like DNS errors and mounted directories
Includes configuration schema (mirrord-schema.json) and structured changelog management (towncrier)
risks: Open issue for Windows ARM64 support indicates incomplete cross-platform coverage
Complexity of network interception and agent coordination may introduce subtle runtime incompatibilities

skeptic.summary: While mirrord claims to enable seamless local development in remote Kubernetes environments, its practical reliability is undermined by unresolved platform gaps, opaque operational complexity, and potential stability risks from deep network interception.
highlights: Despite active releases, a known open issue (Windows ARM64) remains unaddressed, suggesting inconsistent cross-platform commitment
Heavy reliance on low-level network and filesystem interception may introduce unpredictable behavior in complex or non-standard Kubernetes setups
Recent fixes for IPv6 truncation, Unix sockets, and DNS errors indicate ongoing instability in core networking functionality
risks: Unverified claims of seamless AI agent integration lack public validation or performance benchmarks
Operational safety in production-like environments is unclear—ephemeral container usage and agent injection could disrupt workloads despite stated intentions
Dependency on kubeconfig assumes idealized cluster access; real-world RBAC, network policies, or air-gapped environments may break assumptions
